name: UnitedHealth Group
description: UnitedHealth Group is two companies under one roof. UnitedHealthcare is a health insurer (employer, individual, Medicare Advantage, Medicaid plans) that collects premiums and pays medical claims; it made 77 percent of FY2025 consolidated revenue before eliminations. Optum is a collection of health services businesses: Optum Rx (a pharmacy benefit manager and pharmacies), Optum Health (owned and affiliated doctors and clinics) and Optum Insight (data, software and payments). Optum sells largely to UnitedHealthcare and to outside insurers and employers, so segment revenues overlap and $168 billion is eliminated on consolidation. FY2025 revenue was $447.6 billion (up 12 percent) but earnings from operations fell 41 percent to $19.0 billion because medical costs ran above what premiums priced in, plus restructuring and a provider-loan reserve.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code is 6324 (Hospital & Medical Service Plans), from the EDGAR submissions record.

hq.note: FY2025 10-K cover lists two principal executive offices: Eden Prairie, MN 55344 and 655 New York Avenue, Washington, DC 20001

employees.note: About 390,000 employees, nearly 165,000 of them clinical professionals. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: UnitedHealthcare
businessLines.how: Employers, individuals and governments pay fixed monthly premiums per member; UnitedHealthcare keeps the difference between premiums and the medical claims it pays. Profit depends on setting premiums above medical cost trend, and on Medicare Advantage rates set by CMS.
businessLines.description: Health insurance: Employer & Individual, Medicare & Retirement (Medicare Advantage 8.4 million people, Medicare Supplement 4.3 million at 2025-12-31), Community & State (Medicaid).

operatingProfit.note: vs $15,584M and 5.2% margin in FY2024. Share is of consolidated earnings from operations $18,964M

businessLines.name: Optum Rx
businessLines.how: Fee and spread per prescription: it negotiates drug prices and rebates for insurers and employers, fills prescriptions through its own pharmacies and keeps a margin (about 4 to 5 percent of a very large revenue base). Revenue is dominated by pass-through drug cost.
businessLines.description: Pharmacy benefit manager plus home delivery and specialty pharmacies.

businessLines.name: Optum Health
businessLines.how: Mostly a fixed monthly payment per patient (capitation) to manage that patient's total care, plus fees for visits and procedures; profit falls when patients use more care than the payment covers.
businessLines.description: Owned and affiliated physician practices, clinics and care delivery, largely paid through capitation for Medicare Advantage members.

businessLines.name: Optum Insight
businessLines.how: Software subscriptions, per-transaction fees on claims and payments, and multi-year service contracts.
businessLines.description: Data, analytics, software, revenue-cycle and payments services to health plans and providers (includes Change Healthcare).
